title: Heuristic-led KV Compaction Orchestrator and Slab Revival Playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: KV cache fragmentation on multi-tenant GPU pods is increasing tail latency and per-token cost for continuous-batching workloads. Existing eviction heuristics are reactive and cause oscillation under bursty traffic. Goal: Design and implement an orchestrator that applies lightweight heuristics, short-window compaction, and 'slab revival' (selective background coalescing) to reduce fragmentation without violating latency SLOs. Deliverables: 1) Allocation policy that exposes tunable signals (hotness decay, slack windows, slab pin thresholds) and a simulator for offline tuning. 2) A runtime orchestrator that schedules low-priority compaction tasks between continuous-batching windows and honors per-request latency budgets. 3) Telemetry + experiments demonstrating 15-30% reduction in effective KV footprint and <2% added p99 latency. 4) Rollout plan (canary, staged, fallback to current eviction).
comments: 2026-03-01 - Triage: Identified as high impact for tails on chat workloads. Initial spike analysis attached (link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example.com/runs/kv-frag-2026-02).

2026-03-03 - Design sync: Agreed to prioritize a heuristic orchestrator vs full generational GC. Trade-offs: heuristic approach faster to ship, lower implementation risk; GC may be more optimal but requires larger change to allocator ABI.

2026-03-05 - Simulation: Rafael ran a simulator with synthetic bursty sequences (70/30 hot/cold). Results: naive LRU reduced free contiguous segments by 42% vs proposed hybrid-sliding heuristic which preserved 68% contiguous slots. Simulator repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-sim/pull/89

2026-03-07 - Implementation: Started runtime scaffolding (orchestrator service + coroutine-based compaction tasks). Key constraint: must preempt compaction if batch queue length > threshold. Initial prototype in branch feat/kv-orch-783219.

2026-03-09 - Benchmarks: Microbench on rtx-a100-80GB: background coalesce of 128-slot slab took 18ms when scheduled between batches; p50 unaffected, p99 increased by 0.4% when margin thresholds misconfigured. Tweaked scheduler to require 5ms idle window before compaction chunk runs.

2026-03-11 - Security/ops note: Compaction reads may touch customer KV entries; we validated no additional data exfil surface (review by security team: https://confluence.redwood.example.com/pages/SEC-2026-03-KV-COMP).

2026-03-12 - Design review feedback from Eng lead (Maya Singh): request to add hard circuit-breaker that halts compaction based on observed model latency deviation and to emit a detailed compaction telemetry event for post-mortem analysis.

2026-03-13 - Follow-up: Added metrics: compaction.duration_ms, compaction.slots_coalesced, compaction.preempted=true/false, and compaction.trigger_reason. Updated simulator to replay traces from production for more representative tuning.

2026-03-14 - Next steps: finish E2E tests, add canary rollout config in operator manifests, open RFC PR documenting knobs and safety nets (RFC link: https://docs.redwood.example.com/rfc/kv-compaction-orch).
